items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: I mean he didn’t blame Brubeck for it

ctx.x: This is, I’m not sure we can get into this subject at this point, I’ll just throw it out that white musicians often times seem to have more success with a certain style that was created by African-American musicians. Do you think Cecil Taylor was observing the success of people like Dave Brubeck and feeling the unfairness of it?

Yes, he talked about things like that. He did feel that way, that it was very unfair. I mean he didn’t blame Brubeck for it, but he felt like the society will accept, at least a society of people with resources — basically white people — will accept white musicians playing the music over black musicians. And we can see that in popular music very very easily. You know Elvis, whom I did not consider to be a very talented person. I mean I didn’t like the way he sang, I thought he was a very awkward dancer, but…

I see. Well I have enjoyed this conversation so much, and I’ll do something that interviewers really aren’t supposed to do but I’ll do it anyway. Is there anything that you’d like to talk about that I haven’t asked you?
